translation_notes: prefixes: DC->dc, DCTERMS->dcterms, OWL->owl, RDF->rdf, RDFS->rdfs

graph.objects(subject, prop) -> m{ {subject} {prop} ?o }, arity 1: both subject and prop are plain Python loop variables (subject from subjects_to_check, prop from the desc_properties priority list), so both interpolate with {expr} rather than being written as terms -- the same treatment INSTRUCTIONS_403 gives a parameter in subject position, extended here to predicate position since prop ranges over a list built from prefixed-name values (dc:description, dcterms:description, rdfs:comment).

graph.subjects(RDF.type, OWL.Ontology) -> m{ ?s rdf:type owl:Ontology }, arity 1 (single named variable ?s): the trav_one_step idiom for g.subjects(p, o), same construction as g.objects(s, p) with subject and object roles swapped.
@graph graph designates the method's own graph parameter as current for the whole body (bound method extracted as a plain function; self is never read), so every m{ } stays bare.

Preserved a real quirk instead of 'fixing' it: the second (global) loop over m{ ?s rdf:type owl:Ontology } is NOT gated on `ontology_iri` being falsy, despite what its own comment says -- it runs unconditionally whenever the first loop returns nothing, including when ontology_iri was given but that subject has none of the three description properties. fixture.ttl's ex:OntoEmpty and driver.py's call_global_fallthrough_quirk exist specifically to prove the translation keeps this behaviour rather than silently correcting it (which INSTRUCTIONS_403 SS2 forbids as refactoring).

The true zero-solution case (both loops empty, return None) cannot be reached against the shared fixture.ttl: as soon as any owl:Ontology subject with a description exists anywhere in the file, the unconditional second loop -- see the quirk above -- will always find one, whatever ontology_iri is passed. call_zero_solutions() in driver.py therefore builds its own fresh, unrelated, empty Graph() instead (still fresh per side, as fixture_graph is elsewhere) -- the only way to exercise the empty-result branch without contradicting the quirk test.
ex:NotAnOntology in fixture.ttl carries dc:description but is never typed owl:Ontology and is never passed as ontology_iri: the neighbourhood that must not leak into the global search.

repair.driver: Six calls added, on three new small fixtures (fresh per side): fixture_no_described_ontology.ttl (the only owl:Ontology has no description; descriptions on an owl:Class and on a subject linked to owl:Ontology by rdfs:seeAlso: None expected), with ontology_iri None and ex:OntoBare; fixture_second_ontology.ttl (first owl:Ontology without description, then a BNode ontology with rdfs:comment only: the global loop must reach its second subject and last property); fixture_empty_values.ttl (dc:description "" then a second dc:description, plus dcterms) through both loops; and fixture.ttl with ontology_iri="", a falsy str, the type the repository passes (ontology_extractor.py:150).
mutants_killed: global read `?s rdf:type owl:Ontology`: object widened, predicate widened (result shape kept)
global loop limited to its first subject (`[:1]`)
subject of the reads in the global loop and in the first loop widened to a variable (shape kept)
objects limited to the first value (`[:1]`), in both loops
predicate of the reads widened to a variable, in both loops (shape kept)
global loop replaced by [], and gated on `not ontology_iri` (the quirk 'fixed')

optimization_notes: optimized.py: the two identical triple loops (given subject, then every owl:Ontology subject) are merged into one by appending the owl:Ontology subjects to `subjects_to_check` (`+= graph.subjects(RDF.type, OWL.Ontology)`), which keeps the order of the original, including its quirk (the global search also runs when ontology_iri is given but has no description); the list is initialised with a conditional expression instead of an append under `if`. The subjects are now read eagerly, which changes nothing observable (the graph is not modified). Kept: the `if value:` guard and the explicit `return None`.

optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: `@graph graph`, `subjects_to_check += m{ ?s a owl:Ontology }` and `for obj in m{ {subject} {prop} ?o }`, with the three description properties as prefixed names (143 tokens, against 144 with the Python selectors). No exception to the symmetry rule. The ldpy artefact is longer (ratio 1.108) because the translation's header adds five `@prefix` lines next to the unchanged rdflib imports.
header_optimization_notes: optimized_header.py: Literal and Namespace are unused and go; the two imports become `from rdflib import DC, DCTERMS, OWL, RDF, RDFS, Graph, URIRef`.

optimized_header.ldpy: Literal, Namespace and the whole rdflib.namespace import go (`from rdflib import Graph, URIRef`), and `@prefix rdf:` too (the pattern uses `a`); dc:, dcterms:, owl: and rdfs: stay. The notation ratio goes from 1.108 to 0.992.
